hazard_consequence_node.label: Jet fire
hazard_consequence_node.name: Jet fire
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: Use direct quote evidence such as: "a ten-foot high flame coming from a cylinder" and/or "the venting propylene ignited".
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The report mainly analyzes ignition of pressurized propylene venting from cylinder relief devices and the resulting torch-like flame that heated nearby cylinders and propagated the event. That mechanism is best classified as a jet fire. Later cylinder ruptures/explosions were important escalation effects, but they were secondary to the central analyzed phenomenon of ignited gaseous release from cylinders.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: propylene
entity_nodes.explanation: Propylene in returned cylinders was the material that vented and ignited, directly driving the jet fire scenario.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: propylene return area
entity_nodes.evidence: release and ignition of gas from a cylinder in the propylene return area
entity_nodes.explanation: The fire originated in the outdoor returned-cylinder storage section identified as the propylene return area.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Vapor
condition_nodes.evidence: release and ignition of gas from a cylinder
condition_nodes.explanation: The propylene was in gaseous form when it was released and ignited.

condition_nodes.label: Pressure
condition_nodes.name: High pressure
condition_nodes.evidence: internal pressures increased causing the relief device on a cylinder valve to open and vent propylene
condition_nodes.explanation: The cylinder contents were under elevated pressure, which increased further with heating until the relief device opened.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: Direct sunlight and radiant heat from asphalt paving heated returned propylene cylinders
condition_nodes.explanation: High ambient temperature and solar/radiant heating created the thermal conditions that initiated cylinder venting.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.explanation: The released propylene was capable of burning and did ignite.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: Use direct quote evidence such as: "causing the relief device on a cylinder valve to open and vent propylene".
condition_nodes.explanation: Clarify that this node represents the sustained venting release created when the heated cylinder's relief device opened and discharged propylene.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: Low confinement
condition_nodes.explanation: Treat C6 as a contextual setting descriptor for the outdoor release area, not as a direct cause of the jet fire.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Heating of returned propylene cylinders by direct sunlight and radiant heat
event_nodes.evidence: Direct sunlight and radiant heat from asphalt paving heated returned propylene cylinders
event_nodes.explanation: Environmental heating of returned cylinders was the earliest abnormal event that started the accident sequence.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Unknown ignition source
event_nodes.evidence: most likely from a static discharge
event_nodes.explanation: Ignition clearly occurred, but the report identifies only a probable static discharge rather than a confirmed ignition source.
